body.heading: Why yes runs out
paragraphs: The person who always says yes eventually says it with resentment, exhaustion, or a quiet disappearance. None of those are kind — to anyone. A boundary is not a wall; it is information about how to keep the relationship healthy.
People who care about you would rather hear an honest no than a yes that costs you more than you can afford.

body.heading: Saying it kindly
paragraphs: Keep it short and warm: 'I can't this week, and I hope it goes well.' You do not owe a courtroom defence of your limits, and over-explaining invites negotiation you did not ask for.
Expect a wobble of guilt the first few times. Guilt after a healthy boundary is a habit, not a verdict. It fades; the sustainability stays.

description: Saying no feels like the opposite of kindness — done well, it is what keeps kindness sustainable.
